description: Asterverse is developing Field Shift for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Abuja. We’re building a practical tool that helps farmers compare crop rotations using NASA climate data, field context, and farmer priorities. Transparent scoring, map-based location, and plain-language explanations make the trade-offs easier to discuss. We welcome teammates interested in agriculture, Earth science, software, climate data, design, or science communication.
summary:
Field Shift: Rotation Explorer is a farmer-focused decision-support tool for exploring crop rotations in a changing climate. Users locate a real field on the map, choose a crop and priorities, and load NASA POWER daily weather for that location. The app presents climate trends, heat and rainfall signals, a regional rainfall map, and planting-window context, then compares five rotation approaches using transparent rule-based scores for water resilience, soil-health potential, and priority match.

The results help farmers and extension workers identify options to discuss using their knowledge of local soil, water, labour, equipment, and markets. Scores are a shortlist for exploration; they do not predict yield or replace soil tests, field observation, or local agronomic advice. Field Shift makes Earth observation data easier to interpret in a practical farm conversation.
details:
Field Shift helps farmers and agricultural extension workers explore crop-rotation options for a specific location. Users can search for a place, choose it through location selectors, pin it on the map, or opt in to device location. They enter the crop, soil context when known, farmer priorities, and optional observed yield. Observed yield is user-provided context; the app does not use it to predict future yield.

For the selected field and climate period, the app retrieves NASA POWER daily agroclimatology data. It summarizes temperature, rainfall, humidity, and solar radiation; shows climate trends, heat and rainfall signals, regional rainfall patterns, and a planting-window screen; and compares the current rotation with drought-tolerant cover crops, legume mixes, agroforestry, and intercropping. Each option receives a transparent 1–5 score. Overall fit weights water resilience at 40%, soil-health potential at 30%, and match to the user’s priorities at 30%.

The app is designed to make climate information easier to use in a local decision-making conversation. Users can review trade-offs, download comparison notes, farmer cards, SMS-length summaries, or CSV data; extension workers can organize field records. It is a prototype and does not claim proven yield gains or replace local expertise.

Built with Python, Streamlit, pandas, requests, Plotly, Folium, streamlit-folium, and pycountry. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with some code and writing. NASA POWER observations come from NASA; rotation scores are generated by the app’s deterministic rules, not by a generative AI system.
